title: Karol G Reveals New Album’s Tracklist Features Collabs With Drake, Bruno Mars & More
summary: The Colombian artist will drop her sixth studio set, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, soon.
contentText:
Karol G has unveiled the tracklist of her sixth studio album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto, which is set to drop Friday (Aug. 7). 

Related

Karol G Invites ‘Everyone To Be A Little More Dramatic, A Little More Extra’ With New Album ‘No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto’

Karol G Kicks Off 2026 Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour: Full Setlist

Greg Gonzalez on How ‘Después de Ti’ With Karol G Was Born at His Home Bar: ‘A Powerful Moment’

The Colombian artist revealed the song titles in an Instagram post Wednesday (Aug. 5) that featured a baby blue back cover showing a relaxed looking Karol G with her hair flowing around her face. Over the image are the 14 titles alongside the names of featured artists — in order — Drake on “Ahí,” Bruno Mars on “Still,” Judeline and Rusowsky on “Bby Wow” and Greg Gonzalez of Cigarettes of Sex on album closer “Después de Ti.”

If the title of her new set — which translates to “I Don’t Regret Feeling So Much” — is any indication, the project may be a departure from her 2025 album, the tropical-leaning Tropicoqueta , and a more intimate and vulnerable look at the musician born Carolina Giraldo Navarro.

The song names can even attest to all the feeling and passion she poured into this new set, such as “Bebiendo Lagrimas” (“Drinking Tears”), “Alguien Que Te Amaba” (“Someone Who Loved You”) and “¿Con Quién Andará?” (“Who Is He dating?”).

Karol first previewed her new era at her headlining Coachella set in April, where she premiered the nostalgic ballad “Después de Tí” with guitarist Gonzalez, powered by a dreamy, glam pop melody grasping on to the memories after dealing with loss and grief.  She later teased the provocative perreo “Matadora” at the kickoff show of her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour on July 24 in Chicago’s Soldier Field. The song debuted at No. 3 on the Hot Latin Songs chart dated Aug. 8.

And fans may have suspected something could be in the works with the OVO boss when Drake showed up at Karol G’s Toronto show on July 29. Though he didn’t join her on stage at the Rogers Centre, Drizzy did appear on the giant screen, smiling and grooving to her music. Prior to that, Charlamagne Tha God had claimed that the Colombian star was set to appear on Drake’s album ICEMAN , which arrived in May without a collab between the two, though the rapper did give her a shout-out on companion album MAID OF HONOUR ‘s “New Bestie.”
